strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous dataset curation from 15 hospitals with 208,941 cases across 7 anatomical regions
Well-designed instruction-tuning data generation pipeline with expert validation, deduplication, and quality control
Strong empirical results on report generation with 10.15 BLEU-1 point improvement over Qwen2-VL baseline
Thorough experimental evaluation including multiple tasks, anatomical regions, metrics, and ablation studies
Clear motivation and demonstration of the gap between general and ultrasound-specialized VLMs
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty—Dual-path MoE applies well-established techniques without significant methodological innovation
Fundamentally misaligned with ACL scope: this is a medical imaging application paper lacking core NLP/computational linguistics contributions
Unfair experimental comparisons: EchoVLM (11B) compared against 7B baselines, confounding model size with architectural effects
Weak and inconsistent VQA performance (26.52 BLEU-1); shared expert ablation hurts VQA (-4.63 BLEU-1), contradicting its design
Claims of 'universal' applicability undermined by drastically poor vascular performance (BLEU-1: 29.54 vs. 37.62 baseline)
Missing clinical validation: no medical expert evaluation of report quality; BLEU/ROUGE metrics insufficient for assessing clinical correctness
Inadequate treatment of medical data ethics: no discussion of IRB approval, patient consent, anonymization, or fairness considerations for sensitive medical domain
Training data generated by LLMs (GPT-3.5, Qwen, Llama) with risk of error propagation; only 5% sampling verification may be insufficient for medical data
No statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or inter-annotator agreement; single test set evaluation
Dataset availability unclear despite claims; ethical/legal constraints on sharing medical data inadequately discussed

strengths: Comprehensive dataset contribution: Largest multi-organ ultrasound dataset (208,941 cases, 1.47M images, 7 systems) with thoughtful 'redefined desensitization' preserving clinical measurements and anatomical landmarks
Thorough experimental evaluation: Systematic comparisons against 12 baselines across 3 tasks with multiple metrics, ablation studies, entity-level evaluation, OOD testing, and case studies
Strong consistent empirical results: EchoVLM achieves SOTA across most anatomical systems (e.g., BLEU-1: 53.87, ROUGE-1: 61.69 average) with efficiency gains over full-parameter fine-tuning baselines
Well-designed architecture: Principled Dual-path MoE preserving base knowledge while learning domain-specific patterns through two-stage training with parameter isolation and LoRA
Reproducibility support: Detailed configuration tables, implementation details, promised open-source release, greedy decoding for determinism
Clinical relevance: Addresses genuine need for specialized ultrasound VLMs across 7 anatomical systems and multiple clinical tasks
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: MoE application to medical VLMs is engineering-focused, not methodologically innovative; instruction-tuning pipeline builds directly on Self-Instruct; training strategy uses standard LoRA/MoE combinations

Clinical validity concerns: Acknowledges n-gram metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) correlate poorly with clinical correctness yet relies on them; no radiologist validation, inter-rater agreement, or clinical outcome studies; case studies show numerical discrepancies with ground truth not analyzed for clinical significance

Data quality validation gaps: Only 2.2% of 1.8M instruction pairs manually verified; LLM/VLM pre-screening may introduce correlated biases; 47% deduplication rate suggests potential diversity loss; no inter-annotator agreement metrics; desensitization approach privacy implications not addressed

Generalization issues: Poor vessel system performance acknowledged but not investigated or mitigated; limited OOD evaluation (only public KMVE dataset, no external institutions or rare diseases); overwhelming image-token dominance in routing suggests dataset imbalance

Incomplete methodological analysis: No ablation on desensitization approach; hyperparameter choices unjustified (γ=0.001 without sensitivity analysis, shared expert dimension 4× arbitrary); expert specialization analysis superficial; VQA underperformance vs. Lingshu unexplained
Venue fit gap: Fundamentally a medical domain-application paper with limited core NLP/computational linguistics methodological contributions; would be better suited for MIDL/TMI/JAMIA than ACL

Missing clinical deployment elements: No risk stratification, uncertainty quantification, fairness analysis across patient demographics, sensitivity/specificity analysis, radiologist usability study, or regulatory approval pathway discussed

Incomplete transparency: Minimal IRB details despite handling sensitive patient data; train/test split selection method unspecified; potential data leakage from using LLMs for both generation and evaluation; computational efficiency analysis absent (inference latency, throughput, memory footprint)
Statistical rigor: No confidence intervals or significance testing in results tables; case studies claim 'random selection' but limited to 6 anatomical systems due to space constraints
